standard_prerequisites.name: 0-truncation
standard_prerequisites.statement: trunc 0 A is the set of connected components of A, and a map is surjective on 0-truncations when every component of the codomain is hit.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the first hypothesis of the statement and is used at source line 2388 to produce a point a : A.

standard_prerequisites.name: Embedding
standard_prerequisites.statement: f is an embedding when ap f : (x = y) -> (f x = f y) is an equivalence for all x, y.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof observes at source line 2387 that the second hypothesis says exactly that f is an embedding.

standard_prerequisites.name: Characterisation of equivalences by embeddings that are surjective
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map is an equivalence if and only if it is an embedding and surjective.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction performed at source line 2388 and it is the reason the rest of the proof only has to produce surjectivity.

core_obligations: Read the second hypothesis as the statement that f is an embedding, by the definition of embeddings recorded in the retained section reference (source line 2387).
Reduce the goal to surjectivity of f using the characterisation of equivalences as embeddings that are surjective, so that it remains to show trunc(-1)(fiber_f b) for every b : B (source line 2388).
For a given b, use the first hypothesis to obtain a merely existing a : A with trunc 0 f (|a|_0) = |b|_0, and strip the truncation because the goal is a mere proposition (source lines 2389-2390).
From that equality deduce trunc(-1)(f a = b), and again strip the truncation of the goal to assume an actual path f a = b (source lines 2391-2392).
Conclude that the fiber of f at b is inhabited and therefore merely inhabited, which is the required surjectivity (source lines 2393-2394).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the goal to surjectivity by identifying the second hypothesis with being an embedding.
Use surjectivity on 0-truncations to get a component preimage, stripping the truncation of the goal.
Convert the component equality into inhabitation of the fiber and conclude surjectivity.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 8.8.1 at source lines 2378-2385: if trunc 0 f is surjective and ap f is an equivalence on all path spaces, then f is an equivalence. The author's proof (source lines 2386-2394) is short but it is a genuine exercise in truncation bookkeeping rather than a citation: the second hypothesis is first recognised as the statement that f is an embedding (line 2387), which lets the goal be reduced to surjectivity through the retained characterisation of equivalences (line 2388), and surjectivity is then produced in two stages. In each stage the point is that the goal is a mere proposition, so the merely existing data supplied by the first hypothesis may be assumed purely (lines 2389-2392); only after that does the inhabitation of the fiber follow (line 2393). Neither the reduction nor the two truncation strips are visible from the statement.
